title: Verdier trace classes commute with specialization
statement:
Use the finite coefficient and specialization conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions] and [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. Let $c:C\to X\times_kX$ be a correspondence between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $\widetilde c:\widetilde C\to\widetilde X\times_D\widetilde X$ lift it, with special fibre $b=\widetilde c_0$. Let $F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ and define its fixed-locus lift by
$$\widetilde F:=\widetilde C\times_{\widetilde X\times_D\widetilde X,\,\widetilde c,\,\widetilde\Delta}\widetilde X,$$
where $\widetilde\Delta$ is the diagonal of $\widetilde X$; its special fibre is $\operatorname{Fix}(b)$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, and assume that $\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X}K\in D^b_{ctf}(\widetilde X_0,A)$ and that all correspondences and dualizing complexes used are admissible. Then for every $u:c_2^*K\to c_1^!K$,
$$\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde F}\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_{b}\bigl(\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde c}u\bigr).$$
Here $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the Verdier trace class of [def-trf-trace-class], the fixed schemes are those of [def-trf-fixed-scheme], and the specialization on Borel--Moore sections is that of [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. No properness of $c$, $\widetilde c$, $X$ or their fixed schemes is assumed, and no invertibility of $u$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.5, diagram (1.7), with the two legs interchanged; proof §4.3.4

proof.text: Use the canonical nearby-cycle pre-comparison and its proper refinement supplied by [lem-trf-specialization-cohomological-comparison], with the specialization maps of [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. Put $\bar X=\widetilde X_0$ and $F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$. The lift of $F$ is the displayed fibre product in the assertion: on any test scheme its special fibre parametrizes maps to $\widetilde C_0$ and $\widetilde X_0$ with equal images in $\widetilde X_0\times\widetilde X_0$, hence is $\operatorname{Fix}(b)$ by [def-trf-fixed-scheme]; the same argument on the generic fibre identifies it with $F$. The cited comparison theorem supplies the etale representatives, the normalized transported exceptional adjoints, and the finite-Tor domains for every intermediate object.

Factor this pre-comparison into specialization to the proper-refined special fibre, then proper direct image to the original special fibre, using the canonical factorization in [lem-trf-specialization-cohomological-comparison]. For the first factor all structural evaluation, exceptional composition, dualizing and fixed-square identities needed below are supplied by [lem-trf-specialization-structural-identities]. Its fixed-square exchange clause applies because the total diagonal of the separated lift is a closed immersion and so is its base change. The proper-direct-image factor is compactifiable by [lem-trf-proper-direct-image-comparison], and is also covered by the structural-identities statement. Thus the following calculation applies to each factor. We use no unconditional compactifiability assertion for nearby cycles; the current comparison theorem makes that assertion conditional.

The external-product comparison $\Pi$ is invertible for each of these two actual factors. For specialization this is [lem-trf-specialization-external-product], after strict henselization in its stated conventions. For proper direct image it is [lem-trf-proper-comparison-product]: the map is $\mathrm{Ku}_!^{-1}$ with precisely the prescribed exchanges and counits. These inputs justify the cancellation below and assert no tensor-product preservation on a single degeneration.

The formulas in [def-trf-cohomological-comparison] for composing two pre-comparisons substitute their whiskered $\alpha,\beta$ maps into the coefficient comparison and their $j,\delta$ maps into the section comparison. Hence pasting the two commuting trace squares proved below gives the square of their canonical composite from Step 2. This follows simply by replacing each composite transformation by the displayed defining formula and reassociating the arrows; the identity comparison gives the length-zero case. It therefore suffices to do Steps 5--10 for either factor separately.

Fix either actual factor of Step 2, $(f,t,\alpha,\beta,\iota)$, from $c$ to a correspondence denoted $\bar c$, and use its maps of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison]. Put $K'=f_XK$, $P=K\boxtimes D_XK$, $Q=f_XK\boxtimes f_XD_XK$ and $\bar P=K'\boxtimes D_{\bar X}K'$. Let $J=1\boxtimes d_X:Q\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar P$; it is an isomorphism by axiom (V), and the external comparison $\Pi:Q\to f_{X\times X}P$ is an isomorphism by Step 3. Denote by $e_K:P\to R\Delta_*\omega_X$ the evaluation kernel in [lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality]. We claim
$$\bar e_{K'}\circ J=R\bar\Delta_*(\delta_X)\circ\alpha_{\Delta,*}\circ f_{X\times X}(e_K)\circ\Pi.$$
Take ordinary $\bar\Delta^*\dashv R\bar\Delta_*$ adjoints. The right side becomes $\delta_X f_X(\operatorname{ev}_K\circ\mathrm{sym})\alpha_\Delta\bar\Delta^*\Pi$. Clause (c) of [lem-trf-specialization-structural-identities] replaces the last two factors by $t_X$. The transpose defining $d_X$ changes $\delta_X f_X(\operatorname{ev}_K)t_X$ into $\operatorname{ev}_{K'}(d_X\otimes1)$. Axiom (I), naturality of signed symmetry and the symmetry in the evaluation kernel put this into exactly $\operatorname{ev}_{K'}\mathrm{sym}(1\otimes d_X)$, the adjoint of the left side. The adjunction bijection is injective, proving the claim. This compares both the map and its sign.

source.place: §4.4.2, diagram (4.13), with the factors and legs interchanged

proof.text: Use $V=R\mathcal Hom(p_2^*K,p_1^!K)$ and its barred version, with $P,Q,J$ from Step 5. The evaluation-compatible external-duality isomorphism of [thm-trf-verdier-duality] is $\kappa^{-1}$, where $\kappa:P\to V$ is [def-sf-kv-maps](iv). The normalization [lem-trf-projection-kunneth-tensor] identifies its tensor--Hom transpose with evaluation on the second factor followed by $T_{p_1}(\chi\otimes1)$, inserting the signed symmetry to put the factors in the order $K\boxtimes D_XK$. This is the same map, including its counit and sign, that is used in the trace construction; no choice of an external-duality isomorphism is made.

Set $\theta_Z=R\mathcal Hom(\alpha_{p_2},\beta_{p_1})\circ r_{X\times X}$. Apply [lem-trf-external-duality-comparison], whose structural tensor, unit and projection hypotheses hold by [lem-trf-specialization-structural-identities], to get $\theta_Zf_{X\times X}(\kappa)\Pi=\bar\kappa J$. Put $L=R\bar\Delta_*(\delta_X)\alpha_{\Delta,*}$ and $\tau=e_K\kappa^{-1}$. This equality and Step 5 give
$$\bar\tau\theta_Zf_{X\times X}(\kappa)\Pi=Lf_{X\times X}(e_K)\Pi=Lf_{X\times X}(\tau)f_{X\times X}(\kappa)\Pi.$$
Both $f_{X\times X}(\kappa)$ and $\Pi$ are isomorphisms, respectively by [thm-trf-verdier-duality] and Step 3. Cancel their composite to obtain $\bar\tau\theta_Z=Lf_{X\times X}(\tau)$, the full product trace square. The cancellation uses only these actual factors.

Pass from the identity correspondence to $c$. The external-duality trace construction [lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality] factors as the inverse of the exceptional Hom exchange, the exceptional pullback of $\kappa^{-1}$ and $e_K$, and fixed-square exchange. Use $H_c:c^!R\mathcal Hom(p_2^*K,p_1^!K)\to R\mathcal Hom(c_2^*K,c_1^!K)$, the evaluation-defined map of [lem-trf-specialization-structural-identities](b); its isomorphism property is [lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange], in the inverse direction there. The ordinary comparisons of the two legs factor through $c,p_i$ by axiom (III) of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison]; the exceptional comparisons factor through those maps by [lem-trf-specialization-structural-identities](e). Clause (b) of the structural identities, with $g=c$, $M=p_2^*K$, $N=p_1^!K$, is precisely the square that compares $f_C H_c$ with $H_{\bar c}$ through $\beta_c$, $r_{X\times X}$ and the leg comparisons. The remaining lower square commutes by naturality of $H_{\bar c}$ in $M,N$. Paste this square with the diagram proved in Steps 5--7. This gives the comparison through $c^!e_K$; the only remaining arrow is the fixed-square exchange to the dualizing complex on the fixed locus.

Both fixed squares are Cartesian by [def-trf-fixed-scheme]. Since $X,\bar X$ are separated, their diagonals are closed immersions by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Their base changes $i_F,i_{\bar F}$ are closed immersions by [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image], hence these four maps are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. No claim of properness is made for $c,d$ or a structure map. The exchange $B_c:c^!R\Delta_*\omega_X\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_{F*}d^!\omega_X$ is exactly [thm-trf-fixed-point-base-change](2), normalized as the right-adjoint compact-support mate, and the dualizing identification $d^!\omega_X=\omega_F$ is [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]. Apply [lem-trf-specialization-structural-identities](f) with $h=\Delta$, $v=c$, $h'=i_F$, $v'=d$. It compares the inverse of $B_c$ with the inverse of $B_{\bar c}$ via $\beta_c$, $\alpha_{\Delta,*}$, $\alpha_{i_F,*}$ and $\beta_d$. Since both exchanges are isomorphisms, invert these two arrows in this commuting square. Naturality moves $\delta_X$ through the exchange, and clause (e) identifies $d_{\bar c}^!\delta_X\circ\beta_d$ with $\delta_F$. Pasting with Step 8 therefore gives the full sheaf-level trace square
$$\varphi_{\bar c,K'}\circ\theta_C=Ri_{\bar F*}(\delta_F)\circ\alpha_{i_F,*}\circ f_C(\varphi_{c,K}),\qquad\theta_C=R\mathcal Hom(\alpha_{c_2},\beta_{c_1})\circ r_C,$$
where $\varphi$ is exactly the composite in [lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality]. This proves the sheaf-level assertion rather than taking a trace-compatibility theorem as an input.

Apply the preceding sheaf square to the section $\widetilde u:A_C\to\mathcal H_c(K)$ representing $u$, as in [def-trf-trace-class]. For a morphism $q:M\to N$, the tensor--Hom transpose of $r_Zh_Z(q)$ is $f_Z(q)\circ t_Z(1\otimes j_Z)$; this is $f_Z(q)$ by [lem-trf-specialization-structural-identities](c). Thus $r_Zh_Z(q)$ is the section representing $f_Z(q)$. Composing with the two leg comparisons shows that $\theta_Ch_C(\widetilde u)$ represents $\beta_{c_1}f_C(u)\alpha_{c_2}$. Its exceptional adjoint is $f_X(\widehat u)\circ\beta_{c_1,!}\circ R\bar c_{1!}(\alpha_{c_2})$: substitute the definition of the mate $\beta_{c_1,!}$ from [def-trf-cohomological-comparison], move $f_C(u)$ through the unit by naturality, and cancel the exceptional unit--counit pair. For specialization this is the coefficient morphism prescribed in [def-trf-deformation-specialization].

For the output sections, ordinary adjunction gives $h_C$ followed by $\alpha_{i_F,*}$ equal to $h_F$. Indeed axiom (III) yields $\alpha_{i_F}(A_C)\circ i_{\bar F}^*j_C=j_F$, since $a_F=a_Ci_F$. Transposing the two candidates for a section of $Ri_{\bar F*}f_F\omega_F$ now gives this same composite followed by $f_F$ of the adjoint section; the ordinary counit and unit cancel. Postcomposition with $\delta_F$ consequently sends a section $q:A_F\to\omega_F$ to $\delta_F f_F(q)j_F$. By [def-trf-trace-class] these are the two section maps induced by the sheaf square. In the specialization comparison, the maps $j_F$ and $\delta_F$ are respectively the nearby-cycle constant unit and exceptional dualizing comparison, so $q\mapsto\delta_F f_F(q)j_F$ is exactly the Borel--Moore specialization of [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. Steps 1--9 and this section computation, with the pasting in Step 4, prove the stated equality for the original lift. All formulas are linear in the arbitrary $u$; no inversion of $u$ occurs.

split_report.summary: Repair of returned Steps 1 and 3: extracted the proper-product normalization, projection exceptional-Kunneth normalization, and external-duality comparison into three statement-only nodes. A fourth node states the structural identities for the actual geometric specialization factors, repairing the now-conditional compactifiability input without changing the item statement or Lean record. Retained product evaluation, exceptional Hom, fixed-square exchange and section calculations of the returned proof, with renumbering and citations updated.

Steps 1--4 replace the returned setup; Steps 6--7 replace returned Step 3. Original Steps 2,4,5,6 persist as Steps 5,8,9,10. No unit route or statement changed.

tool_uses.why: The generic definitions (ii),(iv) specify the exceptional Kunneth map and its evaluation transpose, needed to compare the exact maps in Steps 6--7.
A generic normalized geometric operation tool required by the displayed comparison; the contraction unit gives no substitute for it.
The explicit normalized external-duality composite defines the trace morphism being compared; the contraction unit gives no replacement trace construction.
The generic evaluation-compatible external-duality isomorphism identifies the product kernel and the internal-Hom source in Steps 6--7.
The generic exceptional Hom exchange identifies the pullback of the product Hom source in Step 8; it is not a contraction-specific theorem.
Separatedness means that the diagonal is a closed immersion, the proper-map hypothesis used in Step 9.
Closed immersions are preserved by base change, so the fixed inclusions are closed in Step 9.
Closed immersions are proper, verifying the four proper arrows in the support square of Step 9.
The generic right-adjoint fixed-square exchange identifies the support arrow in Step 9; the contraction unit supplies no such operation identity.
The generic composition theorem identifies d^!omega_X with omega_F in the support calculation of Step 9.

The item statement is unchanged and is 1.3.5 with the legs swapped; no properness is assumed and u is arbitrary. Steps 1-4: the factorization through b' follows the corrected, now conditional, comparison theorem. Pi is invertible for the specialization factor by specialization-external-product and for the proper factor by the new Ku_!^{-1} identity. Pasting is Rem 4.3.3. Steps 6-7: the new external-duality comparison is the left square of (4.12), proved in 4.4.3 from (IV) for p1, 4.2.4(b),(f), 4.2.2(a) and ♦. The cancellation uses f(kappa) and Pi, both invertible. Steps 5 and 8-10 are old steps renumbered; I checked them against 4.4.2, 4.4.5, 4.4.6 and Cor 4.3.2. New nodes: structural-identities is calculus (a)-(f) for the two actual factors. It is true by Varshavsky's 'local, replace by compactifications' argument, using the proper extension given by the corrected comparison theorem and the existing open-restriction lemmas. Exchange (f) is correctly limited to proper total lifts, and the total diagonal of a separated lift is closed. proper-comparison-product (Pi^p = Ku_!^{-1}) was tested on identities, Y_i = Spec k (cup-product Kunneth) and the empty case. projection-kunneth-tensor is exactly Varshavsky's ♦ = t_{p!}(BC⊗1) against the project's Ku_!-defined alpha, tested at Y = s and X = s. external-duality-comparison was tested on the identity comparison and K = 0. None restates a clause of the item. None duplicates relative-kunneth-counit, external-duality-composition, product-projection-comparison, the open-restriction lemmas or Kunneth-Verdier. There is no cycle and no SGA citation. I accept the tool uses of lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image and thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition as generic tools. Minor issues, none changed: Step 6/7 cite thm-trf-verdier-duality for kappa^{-1}, which is literally thm-trf-kunneth-verdier but is pinned down by uniqueness of the transpose; clause (e) of the structural node is formatted loosely; the new nodes have no lean_audit field.
